meaning:
Λουκᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ
(prob. an abbreviation of Λουκανός; see Lft., Col., 240; ICC, Lk., xviii; Bl., § 29; accusative to Ramsay, Exp., Dec., 1912, pp. 502 ff., a by-form of Λούκιος, from Lat. Lucius),
Luke: Lk, tit., Col.4:14, 2Ti.4:11, Phm 24.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: Luke the beloved physician and Demas greet you.
Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for service.
as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow workers.
